newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - APRIL 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - APRIL 30.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--The General Confederation of Workers of Greece (GSEE) has proposed a special tax which will establish a fund to disburse "social pensions" to those who fail to meet requirements for pension funds and those unable to survive on their income. The idea is one of the proposals to be discussed at forthcoming social dialogue with government and employers.

--Greece telecoms organisation OTE is currently examining its charges policy for the next year with a recent report recommending increases of an average of 2.5 percent on all accounts with local calls carrying an increase of 13 percent.

--Relations between parent-subsidiary companies and holdings of more than 20 percent in financial institutions will be governed by a new framework, as part of Greek legislation's harmonisation with European Community laws. The Council of State is currently considering a new presidential decree on the issue submitted by the national economy and development ministries.
--The annual assembly of the Black Sea Cooperation Council winds up its sessions in Istanbul today.

--The finance ministry is ready to implement a plan to boost tax revenues at the country's eight major tax centres to radically improve the performance of tax collection. The plan foresees covering the shortfall noted in the first three months of the year from April onwards.
--The development ministry will introduce complaints forms at all retail outlets for consumers to note pricing, health and tax irregularities. The measure will come into effect on June 1.

--The general price index at the Athens Stock Exchange yesterday hit a new record of 1,464.75 points, the highest level since August 1990. The continued rise in prices on the ASE is the result of increase investor confidence in the fall of inflation, which is expected to close at 5.8 percent in April.

--The International Monetary Fund's annual check-up of the Greek economy is expected to begin this coming Friday: the IMF is expected to point to inflation at 5.8 percent in April, inflows slightly increased by 60 billion drachmas and public expenditures at 46 percent of GDP, below the Community average.
--Deputy Finance Minister Nikos Christodoulakis has stressed that achieving budget targets is the major "wager" the country is facing at the moment, in an interview with the Wall Street Journal.

--OTE's second share float will be held 10 days earlier than previously scheduled, according to reports. The move has been prompted by the French government's decision to schedule France Telecom's 30 percent share offer for July. OTE's second share offer is now scheduled for the first 20 days of June.

--Industrial units in the Thrace region facing cash flow problems will receive new financial help, according to a recent national economy and finance ministry decision. The businesses will be able to borrow in forex - making lending cheaper - and interest rates will be subsidised by up to 7.5 points.
--The development ministry is planning new incentives to boost ship building and ship repair at Greek yards, in an effort to revive the fleet ahead of the abolition of cabotage in 2004.

--The finance ministry has ruled out any extension to the recent deadline set for the rescheduling of debts to the state. The ministry expected to receive upwards of 500 billion drachmas when the deadline ends on July 31.

--Contacts between the administration of National Bank of Greece and the national economy and finance ministry are now concentrating on the bank's activities in the Balkans. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
